title: Gaps for PLRS with zero coefficients
summary: Zeckendorf proved that every positive integer has a unique decomposition as a sum of non-adjacent Fibonacci numbers. Among its extensions, we focus on Positive Linear Recurrence Sequences (PLRS): fixed depth recurrences with non-negative integral coefficients whose first and last terms are positive: $G_{n+1} = c_1 G_n + \dots + c_L G_{n-L+1}$ with $c_i$ non-negative integers and $c_1 c_L \ge 1$. We again find every integer can be written uniquely as an appropriate sum of terms of the sequence, and we can study the distribution of gaps between summands in decompositions. Bower et al. (2015)…
